headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP interaction: Continue can write shared workspace files while LlamaFactory is non-interactive, making prompt injection and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, and its state is shared via filesystem. LlamaFactory has no direct I/O surfaces, so the main pathway is Continue writing attacker-controlled content that later gets re-read through the shared workspace or MCP. This is plausible in default coding workflows, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF Continue reads content from the shared workspace or an MCP server as instructions
IF LlamaFactory is used to generate content that is later copied into Continue's workspace
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not explicitly needed
Keep the two agents on separate workspaces
Review any file content before feeding it into Continue
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, while LlamaFactory exposes no filesystem, network, or clipboard surfaces. The pair can still leak data if the same workspace contains sensitive files and Continue reads them, but LlamaFactory itself has no path to exfiltrate. The blast radius is limited to local workspace contents.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF Continue is pointed at those files
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict Continue to a narrow project folder
Remove secrets from editor buffers before use
Use local-only model providers for Continue
requires-engineering: enforce file allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but LlamaFactory is marked runnable:false with no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no meaningful write-write conflict between the pair; the only overlap is Continue acting on local files. This makes direct capability conflict unlikely and low impact.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by another runtime that adds write access
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through an external orchestrator
mitigations: Run only one writer per workspace
Keep LlamaFactory non-runnable unless needed
Use separate git branches or folders
Avoid shared mutable state
requires-engineering: add locking around shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code or edits that a downstream workflow may treat as authoritative, and LlamaFactory is a model/fine-tuning tool that could consume copied outputs without verification. The pair does not show built-in verification or coordination, so errors can cascade from Continue into LlamaFactory-driven content generation or training artifacts.
conditions: IF Continue-generated text is reused as training or support content
IF no human or automated verification step checks the output before reuse
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Add a validation checklist for generated artifacts
Keep generated code and training text separate
Mark AI-generated content clearly
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: Continue lists open-source docs and touches source code/editor buffers, while LlamaFactory lists no data classes touched and no residency, retention, or certification claims. Without a documented regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into the shared workflow
IF either agent is configured to process PHI or EU PII
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
Document data-class boundaries
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
Review vendor compliance claims before deployment
